item.title: Coast Guard firefight puts US, Mexico at odds despite coordinated border operations
item.description: A U.S. Coast Guard firefight near the Rio Grande sparked a dispute with Claudia Sheinbaum, who demanded evidence that gunfire came from Mexico.
item.content:encoded:
A firefight involving U.S. Coast Guard personnel along the Mexican border has sparked a dispute between Washington and Mexico City over where the gunfire originated, even as the two countries continue coordinating border security operations.

The Coast Guard told Fox News Digital that personnel conducting joint interdiction operations near Garceno, Texas, came under fire from the Mexican side of the border Sept. 26 and returned fire. No injuries or damage to Coast Guard vessels or equipment were reported, and the incident remains under investigation.

After U.S. Ambassador to Mexico Ronald Johnson publicly announced that Coast Guard personnel had come under fire, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum demanded evidence that the shots originated from her country's territory.

"We asked for all the evidence ​ because we have no evidence," Sheinbaum told reporters in Mexico City, saying Mexican security forces had not detected shots originating from their territory.

MEXICO VOWS US WILL PAY AFTER ICE FATALLY SHOOTS ILLEGAL MIGRANT WHO ALLEGEDLY ATTEMPTED TO RAM AGENT WITH CAR

The State Department, however, told Fox News Digital that information about the shooting had been shared with Mexican authorities.

"U.S. Coast Guard personnel were fired upon from Mexican territory on September 26, and we have shared the available information with the Government of Mexico through official channels," a State Department spokesman said.

The department did not specify what was shared or when, and U.S. officials have not publicly identified the shooters or detailed how they determined the gunfire's origin.

TRUMP DHS HITS 16 STRAIGHT MONTHS WITH 0 RELEASES AT THE BORDER

The incident occurred amid Operation River Wall, a Coast Guard initiative launched in October 2025 to deter illegal migration, drug smuggling and other threats along approximately 300 miles of the Rio Grande.

"Over the past year, the Coast Guard has expanded operations in the region, deploying more than 1,000 personnel and more than 30 assets," a Coast Guard spokesperson told Fox News Digital, referring to "Operation Sable".

Separately, Mexico's Navy Ministry, led by Secretary Raymundo Morales-Angeles, said 159 "Naval elements", 11 vehicles and two drones were deployed to the Tamaulipas sector.

U.S. Northern Command (NORTHCOM) separately told Fox News Digital that American troops are being repositioned to the Rio Grande Valley in anticipation of a seasonal increase in attempted illegal border crossings.

Asked whether Mexico had received evidence from U.S. authorities or launched its own investigation, a representative for Mexican Ambassador to the U.S. Roberto Lazzeri Montaño referred Fox News Digital on Monday to Sheinbaum's more recent remarks addressing the incident.

Sheinbaum said Mexico's military ministry "maintains" communication with NORTHCOM and the Coast Guard and that a "mirror operation" coordinated with the U.S. remains active.

"We want to have a good relationship with the United States within the framework of our sovereignty, our territorial integrity, mutual trust, and coordination without subordination," she said.

Her response did not explicitly confirm whether Mexico had received the information Washington says it shared.

Fox News Digital also contacted Sheinbaum's office for comment.

LATIN AMERICA’S CONSERVATIVE SHIFT FACES ITS BIGGEST TEST YET IN BRAZIL ELECTION

Santiago Vidal Calvo, a Venezuelan-born immigration analyst at the Manhattan Institute, told Fox News Digital that Sheinbaum's approach to border security is shaped by pressure from Washington and a broader Latin American shift toward right-wing governments.

"She has that regional pressure [and] she has the international pressure from the United States" to cooperate on security matters, Calvo said.

He suggested Sheinbaum's demand for evidence of the Coast Guard shooting could reflect pressure within her own political coalition to justify working with the Trump administration.

"She has a high bar to meet if she wants to ally with the Trump administration internally within her own party and her own government," Calvo said.

"We've got to understand this through the lens of what is going on in Latin America. I do think that Sheinbaum's position is substantially different today than it was when Trump got elected," Calvo said.

His assessment reflects Sheinbaum's ties to the left-wing Morena Party and the political legacy of her predecessor, former President Andrés Manuel López Obrador, commonly known as AMLO.

Calvo characterized Sheinbaum as the "last bastion of Latin American socialism," arguing that she could face additional regional pressure if Flávio Bolsonaro defeats President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in Brazil's upcoming presidential runoff.

Calvo suggested that the rightward shift among South American governments could increase pressure on Sheinbaum to cooperate with Washington on security matters.

He said she may face questions about whether "you're the only president of Latin America who's not cooperating with the United States in terms of security?"

"Both of those things do lead to a more serious border campaign for both countries," Calvo said.

"I have no doubt that the change in South America from left-leaning governments to right-leaning governments has to do with the Trump administration's policy in Latin America," he added.

US CHARGES MEXICAN GOVERNOR, TOP OFFICIALS IN CARTEL CONSPIRACY AS MEXICO FIRES BACK OVER PROOF

Border security policy analyst Simon Hankinson told Fox News Digital that gunfire near the Rio Grande is not unprecedented, citing accounts he heard during previous visits to the border.

Hankinson said cartel involvement was possible but expressed doubt that Mexican military personnel would deliberately fire across the border unless they were acting against orders.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"I think these two politicians can cooperate, they can agree on some things, even if they don't agree on socialism versus capitalism and some other ideological issues," he added.

The Coast Guard said the circumstances surrounding the incident remain under investigation.

item.title: Deion Sanders gives bizarre response after Colorado’s offensive script was found at hotel bar before game
item.description: A Colorado staff member allegedly left an offensive play script at the team hotel bar where Texas Tech fans were staying before the game in Boulder.
item.content:encoded:
More than a week after Colorado’s alleged offensive script was posted on social media by a Texas Tech fan during the teams’ game, head coach Deion Sanders is trying to put the embarrassing incident behind him by playing coy about the situation.

This marked the first time Sanders had been asked about the viral situation, which left college football fans scouring game footage in an attempt to determine whether the script was legitimate.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL'S MEGA ROSTERS AREN'T DELIVERING A RETURN ON INVESTMENT, AS LSU, TEXAS A&M AND OREGON ARE PROVING

On the Friday night before Texas Tech faced Colorado in Boulder, Red Raiders fans reportedly came across alleged plays from the Buffaloes’ offensive game plan. That information eventually made its way onto message boards and social media.

When Colorado plays at home in Boulder, the team typically stays at a nearby hotel in the Broomfield area, just a few miles from the stadium. On this occasion, a script of plays was apparently left at the hotel bar, where several Texas Tech fans were also staying.

"A whole playbook. So somebody left a whole playbook, or a script of several plays," Sanders asked the reporter. "I don't think we have a whole playbook, I think they get a script. I thought we scored on the first drive ... So, what's the purpose of the question."

In this case, it's pretty easy to notice that Deion Sanders knew that a mistake had been made by a staffer, which he most likely realized the minute this became a public spectacle. But, this was obviously not a topic that Sanders' was losing too much sleep over.

Or, he was too embarrassed by it all, so deflection was the best route. When asked if he would be further investigating the matter, Sanders hit back with his own questions.

"Why would we, it's over," Sanders started. "Game is over, why would we do that? We probably know a lot more than you think we do. A whole playbook? Come on man."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

When questioned further about the script matching up with the plays Colorado was running on their opening drives, Deion seemingly gave into the fact that someone on the Buffaloes staff left the script inside a hotel bar.

DEION SANDERS TAKES MULTIPLE SWIPES AT HIS CRITICS AFTER COLORADO STUNS GEORGIA TECH

"It happens sometimes. That happens sometimes. I've seen and heard that on the pro level, as well as the collegiate level. But, I think we scored on the first drive, so I guess it didn’t work."

But, the bigger question is why, and if the Colorado coach was concerned with the fact one of his staff members just left a script of plays sitting at the team hotel bar.

"I think if someone had left that, they left it. Mistake, what am I going to do about it? It's over," Sanders proclaimed. "Let's go, let's go. We could have the opposing team's first ten or fifth teen plays, we still have to stop it.

"When you get something like that, do you really trust it as a coach? So was that a dummy script or was that real? Like, that's what your thinking as a coach. If somebody called us and said Utah left the first twenty plays of their script, I wouldn’t believe that."

COLORADO STATE DEFENSIVE COORDINATOR FIRED AFTER DISAPPEARING FROM SIDELINE IN THE MIDDLE OF BLOWOUT LOSS

Ok, as much as Deion Sanders wants to put this whole situation behind him, it's just the latest example of some of the wilder things that have happened over his tenure at Colorado.

And, as we have written over the past few months, the hits just keep building up for those within the Buffaloes football program.

DEION SANDERS DARED THE MEDIA TO WRITE THE TRUTH ABOUT COLORADO FOOTBALL: OK, IT'S TIME TO END THIS CHARADE

But, at least we can read between the lines of what Sanders was implying on Tuesday afternoon.

Yes, it sounds as though a staff member left behind a script of plays intended for the Colorado offense.

No, Sanders was not going to make it a bigger deal than it already was. But if Deion Sanders cannot get things on-track in Boulder, a script might not be the only thing that leaves Boulder.

The clock is ticking on how much longer Deion Sanders is willing to deal with the charade that has overtaken the Colorado football program he created.

item.title: Massive fire destroys 400-year-old food market, leaving historic landmark in ruins
item.description: Flames tore through the Enfants Rouges market in Paris, destroying about 20 vendor stalls inside the historic market founded in 1615. It was the city's oldest covered food market.
item.content:encoded:
Marché des Enfants Rouges, the oldest covered food market in Paris, was engulfed in flames in the early hours of Monday, Oct. 12, destroying vendor stalls and a piece of local history.

The fire broke out around 3 a.m. Monday, with firefighters working for several hours to quell the flames, Reuters reported.

The fire left the market in ruins, with about 20 merchants losing their stalls, according to Ariel Weil, the mayor of central Paris.

CELEBRITY CHEF LEAVES ONE ICONIC INGREDIENT OUT OF HER COOKING AND DINERS CAN'T TELL

"Fire brought under control but market totally devastated. Avoid the area around Rue de Bretagne," Weil said in a post on X on Monday morning.

"9 hoses, including 2 high-powered ones, were required to bring the disaster under control," Brigade des Sapeurs-Pompiers de Paris (BSPP), the city's primary fire and rescue service, said in a post on X.

"150 firefighters were mobilized tonight," Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire posted on X. "I want to express my full gratitude to them."

He added that an investigation is underway to determine the cause of the fire.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"We will find temporary locations for the businesses so that all their activities can be maintained," the post said.

Located in the Marais district of Paris in the city's 3rd arrondissement, the market was founded in 1615 during the reign of King Louis XIII.

A popular destination for both tourists and locals, the market drew people from all over the world, according to the website for the city of Paris.

The name translates directly to "Market of the Red Children," a moniker that came from a nearby orphanage, the Hospice des Enfants Rouges, where the children usually wore red, according to the city's website.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Designated a historic monument in 1982, the market was threatened with demolition in the 1990s when Mayor Jacques Chirac signed off on plans to replace it with a parking lot, a daycare facility and a community center, the Guardian reported.

Before its destruction, the market housed restaurants where people could sit down for a meal or a cocktail.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

A wide range of cuisines were offered, including Moroccan, Creole, Afro-Caribbean and Lebanese, as well as French and Italian, among others.

Although the market was not always food-oriented, it shifted in the early 2000s to center around culinary vendors, including butchers, cheesemakers, fishmongers and a variety of street food stalls, according to the city's website.

item.title: Ilhan Omar’s embattled husband appears at scene of HSI raid in midst of criminal fraud investigation
item.description: Tim Mynett was spotted outside the D.C. home raided by HSI agents as the criminal fraud investigation into Ilhan Omar's immigration paperwork deepens.
item.content:encoded:
The husband of Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., was captured on camera by Fox News Digital entering their shared Washington, D.C., residence the day after it was raided by Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) agents.

Tim Mynett, a political consultant, was walking with a yellow Labrador dog on a leash Tuesday afternoon before entering the home that was searched early Monday morning amid a federal investigation into Omar's immigration status. 

His outing came the same day U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro announced her office is investigating Omar's financial disclosures about reporting of the couple's shared worth.

Two sources close to HSI’s investigation say the raid was part of a criminal fraud investigation into the Somali-born congresswoman's immigration paperwork, which was filled out by her late father when she was a child.

ILHAN OMAR'S WEALTH SCANDAL TAKES A TURN JUST ONE DAY AFTER RAID OF HER DC HOME

Omar’s husband is at the center of one of the congresswoman's most prominent controversies after her financial disclosure filings decreased significantly in reported worth within the span of one filing period.

Pirro revealed her office is now investigating Omar's financial disclosures after the Office of Congressional Conduct in September dropped its misconduct investigation into the congresswoman. Tuesday's announcement opens a new chapter of investigations into the Minnesota Democrat.

The controversy surrounding Omar’s finances began when a 2024 financial report estimated that Omar and Mynett possessed between $6 million and $30 million in assets, all while the Minnesota fraud scandal within the Somali community was beginning to come to fruition.

The largest change in the documents was from Mynett’s assets. His reported ownership interests in both his winery and venture capital advisory firm, which were previously valued in the millions of dollars, are listed with no value now.

In Omar’s 2024 financial disclosure records, Mynett’s share in his winery was valued between $1 million and $5 million, and his share at the venture capital advisory firm was valued between $5 million and $25 million. Now, his equity interests are both listed at $0.

OMAR DUCKS QUESTIONS AS SCRUTINY GROWS OVER FILINGS THAT SLASHED HER REPORTED WEALTH BY MILLIONS

Omar's office previously told Fox News Digital that Mynett has partners in both businesses and said the earlier disclosure mistakenly reflected the businesses' total equity rather than his ownership interest. The office also said the original filing listed assets without accounting for liabilities.

Mynett was a partner of a firm that worked on Omar’s 2020 re-election campaign. The two announced their marriage in March 2020.

This is Omar’s third marriage, but not her most controversial. The "Squad" Democrat has also come under fire for her first marriage to a man many alleged to be her brother. Critics and skeptics claim the two married as part of an immigration scheme.

WATCH: ILHAN OMAR DENIES FEDS HAVE CONTACTED HER AFTER BORDER CZAR HOMAN CONFIRMS 'CRIMINAL' INVESTIGATION

When White House border czar Tom Homan first announced a criminal investigation into Omar, many speculated it would be related to the allegations that she married her brother to evade United States immigration laws. But a former federal prosecutor recently confirmed to Fox News Digital that the statute of limitations would make opening an investigation into the matter difficult.

A Department of Justice (DOJ) spokesperson told Fox News Digital that the judicially authorized search warrant for the raid of Omar’s house Monday was obtained by the DOJ as part of an ongoing federal investigation.

Fox News Digital's Peter D'Abrosca and Amanda Macias contributed to this report.

item.title: Actress Amanda Seyfried rejected TV role over nonstop sex scenes, refused to get 'naked with a stranger'
item.description: Amanda Seyfried says she's no longer willing to be naked with strangers on set, joining Hollywood actresses pushing back against intimate scene demands.
item.content:encoded:
Actress Amanda Seyfried revealed during a Sunday conversation with Alec Baldwin at the Hamptons International Film Festival in East Hampton, New York, that she rejected a television series because of its frequent sex scenes, explaining that she has become increasingly uncomfortable performing intimate scenes as she gets older.

"I passed on a show where I would have to have sex all the time because of the sex. Doesn't matter [who it's with]… I don't want to do it. I'm uncomfortable with it. I'm not into it right now," Seyfried said, according to People Magazine.

Seyfried's decision echoes concerns raised by other Hollywood actresses, including Gina Gershon, who told Fox News Digital in March that she rejected a starring role in the 1981 horror film "Friday the 13th Part 2" after learning her character would appear topless.

"I was offered a lead in that movie," Gershon said, adding that the nudity "definitely felt kind of exploitative to me."

'GAME OF THRONES' STAR LENA HEADEY SAYS OUTRAGE OVER INFAMOUS NUDE SCENE LEFT HER STUNNED

Seyfried, 40, said her feelings about portraying romantic relationships on screen have changed significantly since the beginning of her career, when she was more enthusiastic about filming intimate scenes.

"Maybe if [the project] came along again [at a later point], maybe I'd be in a different space. But I don't want to deal with being naked with a stranger," Seyfried said.

The Oscar-nominated actress previously acknowledged feeling pressured to participate in uncomfortable scenes when she was younger. In a 2022 interview with Porter magazine, Seyfried described participating in scenes without underwear at 19 because she feared upsetting people and jeopardizing her career.

"Oh, I know why: I was 19, and I didn't want to upset anybody and I wanted to keep my job. That's why," Seyfried said.

SYDNEY SWEENEY DEFENDS 'EUPHORIA' NUDITY AND REVEALS A POLE DANCING SCENE WAS CUT FROM SEASON THREE

Other actresses have described similar experiences. In 2023, Christina Ricci revealed on "The View" that she was once threatened with legal action after refusing to perform an intimate scene in a particular way.

"Someone threatened to sue me once because I didn't want to do this sex scene in a certain way," Ricci said.

Keira Knightley previously revealed that becoming a mother changed her willingness to appear nude on camera. The actress incorporated a no-nudity clause into her contracts, allowing her greater control over intimate scenes.

CATE BLANCHETT MOURNS HOW #METOO GOT 'KILLED VERY QUICKLY,' STILL 'SYSTEMIC LAYER OF ABUSE'

Not every actress has taken the same approach. In June, Fox News Digital reported that "Euphoria" star Sydney Sweeney rejected creator Sam Levinson's suggestion to reduce nudity in the show's third season, believing the scenes were relevant to her character's storyline.

Hollywood has introduced additional protections for actors filming intimate scenes. Jessica Steinrock, an intimacy coordinator, told Fox News Digital that coordinators help establish expectations and consent during production.

"[Intimacy Coordinator] is a relatively new role. It really hit its stride kind of in 2018 when HBO made their commitment to having an intimacy coordinator on all their film sets," she said. "An intimacy coordinator is there to provide safety and framework for scenes of intimacy. Those are scenes of simulated sex, simulated genital contact, or scenes of nudity."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Under SAG-AFTRA's guidelines, performers must receive advance notice of expected nudity or simulated sex acts, and producers generally must provide written nudity riders at least 48 hours before filming. The union also established a collective bargaining agreement covering intimacy coordinators in 2025.

Seyfried, who shares two children with actor Thomas Sadoski, said motherhood has further influenced her willingness to establish boundaries, both professionally and personally.

"I have kids now who are paying attention to what I do, and so I have to be less of a pushover," Seyfried said.

item.title: Georgia Tech captain Kyle Efford announces medical retirement from football: 'Nothing left in the tank'
item.description: Kyle Efford led Georgia Tech in tackles three straight seasons before a recurring shoulder injury forced his emotional medical retirement decision.
item.content:encoded:
Georgia Tech standout linebacker Kyle Efford’s playing career is over, but his leadership role with the Yellow Jackets will continue.

Efford announced Tuesday that he is medically retiring from football but will remain a visible presence within the program, retaining his role as a team captain while taking on player-coach responsibilities for the rest of the season.

Efford aggravated his surgically repaired shoulder during a Week 2 matchup against Tennessee. He led the Yellow Jackets in tackles in each of the past three seasons and finishes his college football career with 250 tackles.

MYLES GASKIN RETIRES AT 29 AFTER 7 NFL SEASONS AND A SUPER BOWL WIN WITH THE SEAHAWKS

"Over the past few years, my body has taken more damage than I can continue to ignore," Efford said in a statement. "Damage that will continue to remind me of the sport that I love many years down the road. And while my heart and mind still have so much more to give, I've reached a point where I have to start thinking about the life I have ahead of me."

Efford acknowledged that retirement was not the ending he envisioned but said he walks away without regrets.

"This isn't how I imagined my football career coming to an end, but I am at peace. I can say with complete confidence that I gave this game every single piece of me. There is nothing left in the tank, and there are no regrets in my heart."

Efford leaves the football field with several honors. He was a two-time team captain, earning the distinction in 2024 and 2026. He was also a two-time All-ACC selection, receiving third-team honors in 2024 and honorable mention recognition in 2025. Away from the gridiron, Efford excelled in the classroom, being selected to the All-ACC Academic Team.

He graduated from Georgia Tech in December 2025.

The Yellow Jackets won 30 games and advanced to three consecutive bowl games during Efford’s tenure.

Georgia Tech opened the season with two consecutive losses, including a one-point defeat against Deion Sanders and the Colorado Buffaloes. The Yellow Jackets ended the skid in Week 6 with a 28-25 victory over Duke.

item.title: A Dodgers-less World Series would hurt now, but help MLB later | Bobby Burack
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers are now World Series betting favorites over the Los Angeles Dodgers after taking a commanding 2-0 lead in the NLCS.
item.content:encoded:
For the first time this season, the Los Angeles Dodgers are not the betting favorites to win the World Series. The Milwaukee Brewers, who lead the Dodgers 2-0 in the NLCS, are the betting favorites to win the World Series.

Despite the funeral arrangements demoralized Dodgers are making, Los Angeles isn't eliminated yet. The Blue Jays overcame a 2-0 deficit in the ALCS to defeat the Mariners just last season. Fifteen other teams have done the same.

Those aren't great odds, but as Dodgers fans kept reminding everyone while assembling their superteam, baseball is inherently random. Teams get hot. Players go cold. Great lineups disappear for a week. Struggling pitchers suddenly look formidable. We are not writing off this Dodgers team until someone actually eliminates it.

Even so, the prospect of a Dodgers-less World Series feels real for the first time in a while.

DODGERS DYNASTY ON THE BRINK AFTER THE MILWAUKEE BABIP MACHINE DIALS UP ANOTHER WIN FOR BREWERS

That said, the prospect of a Dodgers-less World Series feels real for the first time in a while.

In the short term, a Brewers-Rays/Guardians World Series would hardly be MLB's dream matchup. As pure a form of baseball as those clubs play, they are small-market teams without much national appeal.

For comparison, the past two World Series featuring the Dodgers, against the Yankees in 2024 and Blue Jays in 2025, averaged around 15.3 million viewers. In 2023, the Texas Rangers-Arizona Diamondbacks World Series averaged just 9 million. A Brewers-Rays/Guardians matchup would probably land much closer to the 2023 number, barring a long, dramatic seven-game series.

However, the long-term gains off the Dodgers missing the World Series could prove worth the smaller viewership this season.

The Dodgers have been World Series favorites for nearly the entirety of the past three years, dating back to the signing of Shohei Ohtani in December 2023. There was a brief stretch during Game 7 of last year's World Series when the Dodgers were trailing and the Toronto Blue Jays had shorter live odds. Los Angeles ultimately came back to win, clinching its second straight championship.

The Dodgers entered 2026 as even heavier favorites than the past two years after adding Kyle Tucker and Edwin Diaz in the offseason. Then, in August, they traded for Tarik Skubal, arguably the best pitcher in baseball.

ESPN MLB insider Jeff Passan likened the 2026 Dodgers to the Avengers, citing their unprecedented collection of star power.

The back-to-back champions adding more stars while much of the league declines to spend or trade aggressively has intensified discussion about a potential lockout and demands for a salary cap. Various outlets — including this one and this author — have argued that the growing disparity between the Dodgers and much of MLB is "ruining baseball."

To be clear, the Dodgers are not at fault for relentlessly trying to improve. They are doing exactly what every fan should want their team to do. The criticism is directed at a system that allows such a competitive imbalance to develop in the first place.

Or, at least, the perception of one.

As the NFL has demonstrated, fans need to believe their team has a chance. It doesn't even have to be true. The same handful of franchises tend to contend for the Super Bowl every year. But constant roster turnover gives most fanbases enough reason to talk themselves into hope before each season.

Jets and Dolphins fans are, of course, excluded from this demonstration.

That becomes harder in baseball when fans suspect their franchise is more likely to trade its homegrown stars to the Dodgers than build around them. The Detroit Tigers' handling of Skubal is an example of that.

There's a reason spoiling movies is considered so obnoxious. People don't want to know the ending before the story begins.

If the Dodgers erase a 2-0 deficit, advance to the World Series and win a third consecutive championship — still the second-most likely outcome of the postseason, according to sportsbooks — MLB will have an increasingly difficult time convincing fans that the rest of the league isn't playing for second place. It will also become harder to argue that stricter payroll rules aren't necessary.

Technically, MLB's scriptwriters would prefer the Dodgers to come back, reach the World Series, and then dramatically lose Game 7. That would deliver the television audience in the short term without reinforcing the idea that baseball's richest superteam is inevitable in the long term.

Still, if we're talking strictly about the long-term health of the sport, the small-market Brewers knocking off perhaps the greatest baseball team ever assembled on paper would suffice.

item.title: ESPN says it's trying to fix a Jason Kelce broadcasting habit that's driving football fans crazy
item.description: Jason Kelce said "we" again during the Philadelphia Eagles-Jacksonville Jaguars London broadcast despite ESPN's efforts to curb the habit, sparking fan backlash on X.
item.content:encoded:
For Jason Kelce, old habits die hard. And for fans outside Philadelphia, they're getting old.

A couple of weeks ago, during "Monday Night Football," Kelce referred to the Philadelphia Eagles as "we" during halftime of their Week 3 loss to the Chicago Bears and ESPN has said that needs to change.

"We’ve tried to get the ‘we’ out of him," longtime ESPN producer Jeff Dufine told the Philadelphia Inquirer.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Dufine noted that using "we" is a common mistake of former athletes and coaches when talking about their old teams.

"We played really well offensively, we had opportunities, we shot ourselves in the foot but we’ve moved the ball, we’ve ran the ball well," Kelce said during the Sept. 28 broadcast.

Pat McAfee didn’t let Kelce’s comments slide, saying, "A lot of ‘we’ talk out of Jason for Philly."

Kelce, who played for the Eagles for 13 seasons, later apologized for his slip-up. The 38-year-old announced the Eagles-Jaguars game in London on Sunday. Addressing his previous "we" comments, he assured Jaguars fans that he would do his best to remain neutral during the game.

"I want to assure Jags fans I’ve seen a lot of the Jags accounts already saying that they’re not looking forward to this," Kelce said on "New Heights." "I will be doing my utmost to give you guys the credit you deserve. Jacksonville’s playing as good as any team right now in the AFC. I really do believe that."

Social media users weren't thrilled with Kelce's performance in the booth Sunday , highlighting the former Eagles star's perceived bias. At one point during the game, when the Eagles punted ball back to Jacksonville, Kelce said "we" punted the ball away.

"Here's an idea. Keep him away from Eagles games," one user wrote on X.

Another was a little harsher, asking, "have they tried getting the Jason Kelce out of the booth?"

"It felt like I was watching an Eagles preseason game," a different fan posted on X.

"ESPN should get (Jason Kelce) out of the broadcast booth permanently," an X user wrote.

Dufine on the other hand praised Kelce prior to announcing Eagles-Jaguars on Sunday.

"He sees the game really well," Dufine said. "Just tell me what you’re seeing, and we’ll support you the best way we can throughout the course of the game."

Kelce’s next assignment is announcing the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints on Oct. 25 in France.

item.title: DAVID MARCUS: On the ground in Middle America, four issues will decide the senate, and none are affordability
item.description: Fraud in Minnesota, growth in Ohio, and culture in Texas are driving 2026 midterm election races more than affordability, ground reporting reveals.
item.content:encoded:
For nearly a year now, the assumption from the chattering classes has been that the 2026 midterm election will be decided on the issue of affordability, but on the ground, in the mid-American states that will decide control of the senate, it is local issues that dominate, not the vague, overarching question of prices.

Part of the problem with nationalizing the affordability issue is that it originated in New York City with the campaign of current socialist mayor Zohran Mamdani. But Gotham is a unique case that is always very expensive. The last time Manhattan was affordable was when the Dutch bought it from the Indians.

In the middle of the country, including Michigan, Ohio, Minnesota, and Texas, all of which this column has visited in the past month, the economy is a major issue, as polls indicate, but it is not the same existential crisis that it was for voters we spoke with in 2022 or 2024.

DAVID MARCUS: IN SPRINGFIELD, OHIO, ONLY TRUMP CAN MEND MAGA-CHAMBER OF COMMERCE RIFT

I met Reggie at a restaurant in Springfield, Ohio. He’s recently married, reading self-help books, and in construction, he told Fox News Digital, "There’s work, wages are good, that’s not an issue, prices are prices, and gas has gone down with the tax holiday."

Reggie was referring to Ohio’s decision to temporarily suspend gas tax, resulting in a price under four dollars in the Buckeye State.

DAVID MARCUS: IN DAYTON, OHIO, BOTH PARTIES FACE BITTER POLITICAL DESPONDENCY

In fact, in no state this column visited did it seem as if cost of living was the prime driver of the electorate. So what is it? Let’s take it state by state.

The cleanest and clearest way to know what issue is driving any community of voters is when they bring something up before you do, and in Minnesota, almost everyone I spoke with brought up fraud with no coaxing.

DAVID MARCUS: PEGGY FLANAGAN'S DEI RECORD AND FRAUD SCANDAL PUT MINNESOTA SENATE RACE IN THE SPOTLIGHT

Over the past year, the scope and scale of fraud in Minnesota’s Somali community has come to shocking light and it is something that Democratic Lt. Gov. and Senate candidate Peggy Flanagan cannot escape, and that her GOP challenger, Michelle Tafoya is rightfully milking like a top-prize heifer at the Minnesota state fair.

This is a race that almost nobody expected to be competitive just a few months ago, but that is because pundits were reading the national mood, not the mood in Minnesota, which can only be found on the ground, and which is very angry.

Dayton, Ohio is full of absolutely lovely people, many of whom I spoke with, and I wish I could say kinder things about it, but it is an all but a dead city. Stunningly beautiful buildings sit abandoned, like coarse reminders of better days.

What Daytonites, as well as Ohians in general, want and need is growth. It's not that they can’t afford their lives, it's that their communities do not thrive, do not grow, and they want to know if a once great state can be great again.

THE BLUE WAVE LOOKS REAL UNTIL YOU LOOK A LITTLE CLOSER

In the race between Republican incumbent Sen. John Husted and Democrat Sherrod Brown, the winner will be the one who can convince Ohio voters that they have a plan to bring cities like Dayton back.

Compared to Dayton, Ohio, Grand Rapids, Michigan seems like Oz. As my Uber driver told me on the drive in, "Everyone I take back to the airport raves about the city. You will, too." And here we are.

Like Detroit, which this column also recently visited, Grand Rapids is a buzzing town, neat-necktied producers of wealth roam the streets discussing deals and going to lunch. You also see kids in a downtown that screams not just wealth, but authenticity.

LIZ PEEK: TWO TROUBLED SENATE RACES COULD SPOIL DEMOCRATS' BLUE-WAVE FANTASY

In the race between Republican Mike Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed for senate, the primary issue is who can sustain the growth that Michigan has experienced, and who gets the credit: Democrat Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, or President Donald Trump.

Texas is another state where the most pressing issue is not economic, but rather, in this case, cultural. Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton has universally been tagged as the worst candidate of 2026, and yet not only is he a successful attorney general, he is also undeniably Texan, for all his big faults.

In James Talarico, Democrats have a once vegan, Unitarian-style Christian, who has admitted his biggest concern in life is making sure trans kids can get access to controversial surgical procedures. Now that Talerico is back from his two week bout of the flu, the cultural questions will be coming hot and heavy, and he has no good answer for them.

EVERYONE IS WATCHING TEXAS AND MICHIGAN. AS A POLLSTER, I KNOW WHERE THE REAL STORY IS

When it comes to the economy, Americans are not in fear, but they do have questions and doubts. When I was talking with Reggie in Springfield, Greg came in. He sells autonomous lawn mowers to golf courses and commercial parks.

Eventually Reggie, who again, is in construction, asked a bit nervously, "How good are the autonomous forklifts getting?"

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Greg confirmed that the forklifts were getting very good, but added something interesting. "A landscaping company doesn’t make money off the guy on a mower," he said, adding, "They make money from the guy trimming and edging. Now that's two guys and you can do an extra job every day."

I’m not sure Reggie was fully convinced or relieved. I’m not sure if I was for that matter, but this is the level of economic anxiety that exists in Middle America, not dread over whether food can be put on the table.

These four key senate races will be won by the candidates who best understand the local issues in their states, not the ones who wow on national TV over zeitgeist issues, and right now, in all four, it is the Republicans who have the upper hand on those issues.

item.title: 'Squad' Democrat formally introduces bill to abolish ICE, Border Patrol and dismantle DHS
item.description: The sweeping bill would ban federal border wall funding, close Guantanamo Bay and dismantle Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Delia Ramirez, D-Ill., formally introduced sweeping legislation to dismantle the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), abolish Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and eliminate Customs and Border Protection (CBP), advancing a radical proposal that would fundamentally overhaul federal immigration enforcement.

The progressive "Squad" member's Reimagining Safety Act would replace DHS with a new Department of Community Safety, while preserving several existing federal agencies such as the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) and Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA).

The legislation would eliminate CBP, including Border Patrol, toppling the federal agency responsible for securing America's borders and screening travelers and goods entering the country.

'SQUAD' DEMOCRAT SLAMMED BY TRUMP ADMIN FOR MOST 'RADICAL' PLAN TARGETING ICE YET

While certain customs and immigration functions would be transferred to other federal departments under Ramirez's legislation, the proposal would eliminate CBP's existing enforcement structure.

The bill's original cosponsors include fellow "Squad" member Rep. Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich., along with Reps. Adelita Grijalva, D-Ariz., and Jim McGovern, D-Mass., according to Ramirez's office.

The legislation would also prohibit federal funding for border walls beginning in fiscal year 2027 and require the closure of the military detention center at Guantánamo Bay within 60 days of enactment.

DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin previously blasted the proposal in an exclusive statement to Fox News Digital last month.

DEMOCRAT COMPARES ICE TO 'DOMESTIC TERRORISTS' AS 111 HOUSE DEMS DEMAND TEXAS DETENTION CENTER CLOSE

"Radical leftists are calling to defund the police and abolish DHS. It’s NEVER going to happen. Our 270,000 DHS patriots are keeping Americans SAFE— unlike this open-borders politician who refuses to prioritize Americans over illegal aliens," Mullin said.

A DHS spokesperson also criticized Ramirez, saying she "should be thanking our law enforcement for removing these dangerous criminals from her district — NOT vilifying law enforcement."

Ramirez previously defended her proposal in a statement to Fox News Digital, arguing the current department should be dismantled and replaced with an agency focused on community safety.

'SQUAD' MEMBER CALLS DHS 'GREATEST THREAT TO OUR SAFETY' AFTER ICE-INVOLVED SHOOTING

"Every day, Americans wake up with a new reason to dismantle DHS, reimagine safety and build something that honors our shared humanity," Ramirez said.

Under the legislation, the TSA and Coast Guard would be transferred to the Department of Transportation, while FEMA and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency would move to the proposed "Department of Community Safety."

Customs functions would hypothetically move to the Treasury Department, while certain immigration functions would transfer to the Justice Department.

The legislation would need to pass Congress and be signed into law before taking effect. None of its proposed changes to immigration enforcement are currently in force.

Elizabeth Elkind contributed to this reporting.

item.title: 'Moonshiners' stars challenge notorious warning that outlaw liquor can make you go blind
item.description: Mark Ramsey and Digger Manes from "Moonshiners" challenge stereotypes about Appalachia's distillers as home distilling battles reach the Supreme Court.
item.content:encoded:
Moonshine’s reputation is enough to make your eyes water.

For generations, Americans have been warned that the notorious outlaw liquor could leave them blind. But "Moonshiners" stars Mark Ramsey and Eric "Digger" Manes say there's more behind that warning than most people realize.

"There's a huge different thought process behind moonshine than there was, say, in the '40s, '30s, early years," Manes told Fox News Digital.

KENNY LAW, 'MOONSHINERS' STAR, DEAD AT 68

"There was a lot of propaganda out there. It was said that it could make you go blind, make you die, make you go crazy, make you get the jack leg. The government was the one that was poisoning the industrial alcohol the people were stealing to make bathtub gin."

Historical records support part of Manes' account. During Prohibition, the federal government required industrial alcohol to contain toxic additives to discourage people from drinking it, according to the Smithsonian Channel. Some of that alcohol was diverted into the illegal liquor market and sold for consumption, although it was distinct from traditionally distilled moonshine.

The consequences were deadly. According to the Smithsonian Channel, 66 people died in New York City on Christmas Day 1926 after consuming poisoned industrial alcohol. The city's medical examiner, Charles Norris, blamed the federal government's practice of adding toxic substances to industrial alcohol, including those involving methyl alcohol, also known as methanol, which can cause blindness and death.

WATCH: ‘MOONSHINERS’ STARS REVEAL THE TRUTH BEHIND A MISUNDERSTOOD TRADITION

But not every warning about illicit liquor was a scare tactic.

Ramsey acknowledged that moonshine posed genuine health risks in earlier generations, particularly when distillers unknowingly used dangerous materials to build their equipment.

"Back in the day, there were people who had health issues because of moonshine," Ramsey explained. "The solder that they used to build the pots had lead in it back in the day, and they didn't know that it was happening. So once it was discovered that the solder had lead in it, even the old timers here, when they built their stills, they no longer soldered their joints on the inside of the pots. All the solder connections were on the outside where the mash never touched the solder anymore."

"So yeah, it caused some issues, but it was strictly an accident," he said. "They just didn’t know any better."

While moonshine does not inherently cause blindness, improperly produced spirits can contain dangerous levels of methanol, a toxic form of alcohol. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention warns that methanol poisoning can damage the optic nerve, causing permanent vision loss or death.

"Moonshiners," which is now in its 16th season, premiered in 2011. The series follows "a diverse group of people living in Appalachia who carry on a 200-year-old tradition passed down from their forefathers, making moonshine," according to the show's synopsis.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Distillers can legally produce and sell spirits marketed as moonshine if they comply with federal, state and local licensing, taxation and other requirements. Federal law generally prohibits producing distilled spirits at home for personal consumption, according to the Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau, although recent court rulings have challenged the constitutionality of certain restrictions.

According to The Washington Post, federal appeals courts have issued conflicting rulings on a federal restriction on home distilling dating back to 1868.

In April 2026, the 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that a federal restriction prohibiting distilled spirits plants from operating in homes and certain other locations was unconstitutional. Days later, the 6th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals reached the opposite conclusion, upholding the restriction as a "necessary and proper means" of collecting liquor taxes, the outlet reported.

The Hobby Distillers Association and four individual plaintiffs challenged the restriction in the 5th Circuit case, according to The Washington Post. Supporters of legal home distilling hope overturning the restriction could spark a "craft spirits revolution."

The legal battle has since reached the Supreme Court. In July, John Ream, the plaintiff in the 6th Circuit case, asked the justices to review the ruling. The Justice Department filed a separate petition in August, seeking to overturn the 5th Circuit's decision.

Ramsey also challenged longstanding stereotypes about "moonshiners."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"A lot of times, people give it a bad name because they just see it as poison and a bunch of heathens out doing stuff they shouldn’t do," he said. "And moonshiners, as a rule, are very, very good people. They were just simply doing what they had to do to survive back in the day."

"[Moonshine] didn't actually sell in Appalachia," Ramsey said. "It went farther north: Ohio, Detroit, New York, the East Coast. ... One of my friends told me ... he took a load of liquor to Ohio and said, 'Them fellas up there, they get it. And every one of them said, 'God bless them hillbillies.'"

"The liquor business back in the day, the heyday of it, probably wouldn't have flourished here in Appalachia so prominently had it not been for our northern neighbors buying it," Ramsey said. "So we had a reason to make it, and they had a reason to want it."

"We were broke, but could make liquor," Manes added. "And they had money and could buy it."

Ramsey is also optimistic about the future of moonshine. He said a new generation of distillers is eager to carry on the tradition.

"As we saw in previous seasons … we always want to know who's going to fill our shoes, who's going to carry the torch forward," he said. "[And] we have so many good distillers up and coming. I think it's got a future, a very healthy one. Things will change. It's been argued that the best drink of liquor hasn't been made yet, so they've got something to shoot for."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"That's the most beautiful thing about the lessons you learn from these old timers that taught you how to make liquor," Manes said. "You make do with what you've got, and you don't let the situation you're standing in drag you down. You keep going forward."

For Manes, preserving the tradition comes down to pride in his craft.

"To me, it's more the pride," he said. "It's no different. I don't know what hobby you may have. It may be painting. You may paint pictures. Well, if you do a beautiful portrait, and you stand back, and you look at it, you think, 'Wow, that really does look good.'"

Manes said he gets that same satisfaction from turning simple ingredients into moonshine.

"We take what other people would consider slop — that’s the conglomeration of cornmeal and sugar — and make a crystal-clear product that tastes good," he said. "And we love it."

"Good thing about this business is it [doesn't] really have bad times," Ramsey said.

"If you’re down in the dumps, you drink to drown your sorrows," he joked. "If you’re happy, you drink to celebrate. So it’s got a good source of customers all the time."

item.title: Popular erectile dysfunction pill may deliver additional boost to aging men
item.description: Tadalafil boosted muscle precursor cell survival in a lab study, but researchers say the active Cialis ingredient also delayed mature muscle development.
item.content:encoded:
Researchers in Italy have discovered a potential association between the common erectile dysfunction drug Cialis (tadalafil) and muscle regeneration.

The study, published in the journal Molecular Biology Reports, tested the drug on mouse muscle cells in a laboratory.

Over a seven-day period, the researchers looked at how the drug affected muscle cell growth, survival and development.

VIAGRA COULD DO MORE THAN ADVERTISED AS STUDY REVEALS SURPRISING HEALTH SUPERPOWER

Tadalafil was found to increase the number of muscle precursor cells, which are involved in the early stages of muscle formation, and helped more of them survive.

The drug also showed signs of helping muscles repair themselves by encouraging growth and reducing cell death.

Despite these positive outcomes, the research found that tadalafil delayed the development of fully mature muscle cells.

This suggests that the drug could create and maintain more cells involved in muscle regeneration but does not indicate an increase in muscle size and function in humans.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Because the study was conducted in mouse models, the results may differ when applied to humans, posing a limitation to the study findings.

The study lasted just seven days, so more research is needed to understand the drug's long-term effects, the researchers acknowledged.

Study co-author Dr. Cristina Antinozzi, a researcher in the Endocrinology Unit at the University of Rome Foro Italico, said these findings represent an "encouraging look at how tadalafil might be repurposed to support muscle tissue repair and regeneration."

"While more work is needed, this research opens up exciting new possibilities for future therapeutic strategies in muscle recovery, though it also highlights the need to monitor how such mechanisms might be viewed or misused in sports and performance contexts," she told Fox News Digital.

Dr. Kien Vuu, a radiologist and founder of VuuMD Performance and Longevity in Los Angeles, who was not involved in the study, agreed that this is an "intriguing early finding."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"In mouse muscle cells studied in a laboratory, tadalafil — the active ingredient in Cialis — helped muscle precursor cells grow and survive, but also delayed their maturation into muscle fibers," he told Fox News Digital.

"That's a fascinating biological signal, but it's far from proving that Cialis builds muscle or improves recovery in people.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"Successful regeneration ultimately requires those cells to mature and form functional muscle tissue. This experiment didn't establish that outcome."

Vuu said this is "worth studying" from a longevity perspective because age-related muscle loss contributes "significantly" to frailty, metabolic dysfunction and loss of independence.

"However, this was a laboratory cell study, not a clinical trial," he said. "We need animal studies and eventually human trials examining actual muscle mass, strength, physical function and safety before drawing conclusions about clinical use."

Lifestyle practices such as resistance training, adequate protein and quality sleep remain the "most reliable ways" to protect muscle with age, Vuu added.

The expert noted that tadalafil also carries "meaningful risks," including dangerous blood pressure reductions when combined with nitrates.

"So, people should not take it for muscle-building based on these findings," he said.

item.title: NCAA softball player alleges person threatened to come to her school and kill her over women's sports activism
item.description: Kendall Kotzmacher says she reported a kill threat to her Colorado Christian campus after speaking out against transgender athletes in girls' sports.
item.content:encoded:
NCAA softball player Kendall Kotzmacher says she reported a threat to come to her college and kill her amid backlash over her advocacy against transgender athletes competing in girls’ and women’s sports, while online targeting has also spread to her teammates.

The 20-year-old Colorado Christian University sophomore, recently named a Courage Wins Champion by XX-XY Athletics, told OutKick that the hostility has intensified as her public profile has grown.

"I had a person say that they were gonna come to the school and kill me. That one was a little scary," Kotzmacher said.

Kotzmacher said she reported the threat to her school and had documented other concerning messages over the summer. Asked whether anyone had been arrested, she said no.

"I’ve been getting a lot of people telling me to go kill myself or that I don’t deserve to be alive or that I should die, a bunch of stuff like that, which has been really difficult to hear," she said.

FINAL SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM RALLY OF THE 2026 REGULAR SEASON PITS SUPPORTERS AGAINST TRANS ACTIVISTS IN MINNESOTA

Knowing that strangers can identify where she attends college has added to her fear.

"I think people knowing where I go to school has been a little bit scary just because I never know if someone’s going to show up or what’s going to go on," she said.

The backlash has also left Kotzmacher concerned about the teammates who publicly support her. She said one person replied to teammates’ comments on her social media posts, visited their accounts and looked up their names and statistics.

"I think I want to protect them as much as possible," she said. "So trying to make sure that they’re not getting any of the backlash and that it’s kind of just on me has been a focus of mine."

Kotzmacher said she offered in the team’s group chat to remove their names from her social media and make clear they were not involved in her advocacy.

Her teammates rejected the offer, she said.

"And they’re like, absolutely not. Like, we’re in this together. We’re going to be supportive of you," Kotzmacher recalled. "Like, we’re all here for you, which has been so refreshing to hear because I didn’t really get that last year."

Kotzmacher, a sophomore catcher and infielder who previously attended Western Michigan University, transferred this past summer after

In her September Fox News op-ed, she attributed her transfer from Western Michigan to a lack of coaching support and pressure in coursework.

Her advocacy began after White Bear Lake High School lost 3–2 to Champlin Park in the 2025 Minnesota Class AAAA state semifinals. Champlin Park, whose team included a transgender pitcher, subsequently won the championship.

Kotzmacher helped put White Bear Lake into that semifinal, hitting a seventh-inning, two-run home run in a 3–1 quarterfinal victory over Farmington.

More than a year later, she is balancing college softball and classes with an increasingly public role in the debate over sports eligibility.

DEMOCRAT SENATORS FLEE OR NO-SHOW JUDICIARY COMMITTEE HEARING ON PROTECTING WOMEN'S SPORTS

She practices four days a week and attends classes daily, she said, while trying to find time for advocacy that has taken her to Washington.

item.title: Prepare yourself for a look at a rare albino caribou calf photographed possibly for the first time
item.description: A biologist's photos capture an albino caribou calf with red eyes and pink hooves north of Fairbanks, Alaska — the first images of one in nearly 50 years.
item.content:encoded:
You want your OutDoors with a story? How about this one? A rare albino caribou calf was photographed recently in Alaska for what very well could be the first time.

Jordan Pruszenski, an Alaska Department of Fish and Game biologist, was counting caribou calves in a small plane north of Fairbanks when she spotted a white speck.

The late June routine activity to determine how many calves survived their first month was about to become anything but routine. The white speck was a rare albino caribou.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

"I’m just like, 'What is happening'" Pruszenski said, reports KOTZ. "You could totally see it like on the horizon, and then it steps onto like the snow patch and totally disappears."

The pilot turned the plane back towards the animal for another look. As the plane took another pass, Pruszenski snapped several photos. In addition to the white fur, this calf also had "incredible, beady red eyes" and pink hooves.

This rare sighting came with even rarer photographic evidence.

The Alaska Department of Fish and Game's last record of an albino calf was from 1976. It had been observed through a spotting scope for a couple of minutes and no photos were taken.

WILDLIFE PHOTOGRAPHER STAYS ICE-COLD AS MASSIVE BROWN BEAR WALKS RIGHT UP TO HIS CAMERA

As for this calf, there's no way of knowing if it has survived past the one-month check in late June. Biologists didn't collar the calf or the mother and its white fur is going to make it stand out to predators.

"Once it steps off of the snow it just really stands out," Pruszenski said. "So we’re really not sure how long it’ll last."

The name of the albino caribou's herd isn't being shared, so that people don't head out on their own looking for it.

"If you happen to see it, it’d be great to let us know. But what we don't really want is people to really be sort of trying to bother this caribou," Pruszenski told the outlet.

"We want to be able to give it its best shot, which will be to kind of just let it be a normal caribou."

That sounds perfectly reasonable. Let the caribou do caribou stuff. It's not looking for fame. Enjoy the photos of the rare animal and keep it moving.

item.title: Ilhan Omar's wealth scandal takes a turn just one day after raid of her DC home

item.content:encoded:
U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro revealed Tuesday that her office is investigating Rep. Ilhan Omar's financial disclosures, opening a new chapter in the controversy surrounding the Minnesota Democrat's previously reported multimillion-dollar assets.

Speaking on Fox News' "America Reports," Pirro said her office was examining Omar's financial disclosures, which previously showed that the reported value of businesses tied to her husband, Tim Mynett, had surged from as much as $51,000 in 2023 to as much as $30 million in 2024.

The latest development comes one day after federal agents searched Omar's Washington, D.C., home as part of an ongoing criminal investigation involving her immigration paperwork, two sources familiar with the probe told Fox News Digital.

The Justice Department confirmed that Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) agents executed a judicially authorized search warrant Monday as part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation. It remains unclear whether the search is connected in any way to the financial disclosure investigation described by Pirro.

WATCH: ILHAN OMAR DENIES FEDS HAVE CONTACTED HER AFTER BORDER CZAR HOMAN CONFIRMS 'CRIMINAL' INVESTIGATION

The disclosures drew scrutiny from congressional Republicans, including House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer, R-Ky., who requested financial records from two companies tied to Mynett in February.

The original filings, examined by Fox News Digital earlier this year, showed millions of dollars in newly reported assets associated with two of Mynett's business ventures — a California-based winery and a Washington, D.C.-based venture capital firm.

ILHAN OMAR NOT OUT OF THE WOODS DESPITE FINANCIAL DISCLOSURE REVISION, TOP REPUBLICAN WARNS

The winery, eStCru LLC, saw its reported valuation jump from between $15,000 and $50,000 in 2023 to between $1 million and $5 million in 2024. Rose Lake Capital LLC showed an even sharper increase, rising from a reported value of between $1 and $1,000 in 2023 to between $5 million and $25 million the following year.

Combined, the businesses had reported values ranging from approximately $15,000 to $51,000 in 2023, compared with between $6 million and $30 million in 2024.

Financial disclosure forms report assets in broad ranges rather than exact dollar amounts, meaning the filings did not establish the couple's precise net worth.

In February, Comer requested documents and communications related to the finances of eStCru LLC and Rose Lake Capital LLC, raising questions about the dramatic increase in their reported valuations.

Omar subsequently amended her financial disclosures in April, reducing the couple's combined reported assets to between $18,004 and $95,000. The revised filing listed her husband's two businesses as having no net value after accounting for liabilities.

Omar's office, at the time, said the original disclosures had failed to properly account for liabilities associated with her husband's businesses, creating what it described as a misleading picture of the couple's finances.

The congresswoman has repeatedly maintained that she is not a millionaire.

MEET THE LONGTIME BIZ PARTNER OF ILHAN OMAR'S HUSBAND AS QUESTIONS SWIRL OVER HER SKYROCKETING NET WORTH

In September, the Office of Congressional Conduct voted 5-1 to recommend that the House Ethics Committee dismiss misconduct allegations stemming from the financial disclosures.

The congressional watchdog found there was not substantial reason to believe Omar had reported false or incomplete information in violation of federal law or House rules.

Omar's office characterized the findings as vindication, maintaining that the congresswoman had done nothing wrong.

The congressional watchdog's review is separate from the federal investigation described by Pirro on Tuesday.

Omar's latest annual financial disclosure, filed in May, listed assets totaling between approximately $20,000 and $125,000, according to a Minnesota Star Tribune analysis. The filing also reported student loan and credit card debt associated with her husband.

The Somali-born congresswoman has denied allegations of wrongdoing and has accused the Trump administration of targeting her for political reasons — especially after Monday's raid of her Washington, D.C., residence.

The Minnesota Democrat has been a frequent target of criticism from President Donald Trump and congressional Republicans.

item.title: PSG’s Luis Enrique Hopes Man City Avoids Sanctions After Financial Rules Verdict

item.content:encoded:
Paris Saint-Germain coach Luis Enrique came to Manchester City's defense on Tuesday, saying he hopes the club won't be stripped of titles after being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules.

Back-to-back Champions League winner PSG plays City at the Etihad Stadium on Wednesday.

City could face sanctions including a huge fine, points deductions or even expulsion from England's top flight. There have also been calls for it to be stripped of trophies it won during a nine-year period in which it was found to have artificially inflated its revenue by more than $1 billion.

"I hope everything works out well for Man City because I think what they have done on the pitch has been incredible over the last few years and they certainly deserved to win all the trophies they have won," Luis Enrique said ahead of the Champions League game. "The trophies you win on the pitch remain on the pitch. They deserved to win that and I hope they can avoid the sanction.

"But now we have to wait to see what the authorities decide or the judge is going to say."

City is under Abu Dhabi ownership and PSG is Qatari-backed. Both clubs have been sanctioned by European governing body UEFA for breaching Financial Fair Play regulations in the past.

City is accused of providing misleading information about its finances from 2009-18. During that time, it won three titles. It has appealed the verdict.

City defender Ruben Dias said the players were focusing on the pitch, like they did Sunday in a 3-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield.

"I feel like when you build yourself as a player, you build yourself against any kind of noise," he said. "Personally, and I really feel like I speak for the whole group, we’re very calm. We trust the club, we’re very calm and we’re very focused on enjoying football."

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: New evidence debunks Talarico psych hospital rumor after ‘mind-numbing malpractice’ fuels firestorm
item.description: James Talarico's campaign provided security footage to debunk the Ohio rehab rumor, but critics ask why the evidence wasn't released sooner.
item.content:encoded:
A viral rumor claiming Texas Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico secretly spent his recent campaign absence at an Ohio behavioral health center has now been debunked — but new questions are emerging over why evidence that could have quickly undercut the allegation was not made public as the speculation exploded online.

The New York Times reported Monday that it reviewed time-stamped security camera images provided by Talarico's campaign showing the Democrat at his Austin home between Oct. 1 and Oct. 8, when his nine-day absence from the campaign trail was fueling mounting speculation about his whereabouts.

The images, which the campaign provided to the Times on the condition they not be published for security reasons, offer the clearest independent evidence yet supporting Talarico's account that he was home recovering from the flu and contradict claims that he instead traveled more than 1,000 miles away for treatment at an Ohio behavioral health center.

PAXTON’S ESTRANGED WIFE BREAKS SILENCE ON TEXAS SENATE RACE AFTER 'BIBLICAL GROUNDS' DIVORCE

But the revelation has also prompted criticism from some observers questioning why Talarico's campaign did not provide similarly verifiable evidence earlier before an unsubstantiated theory about his whereabouts mushroomed across social media and was amplified by prominent conservatives.

"In October of an election year, every day and every hour count as candidates do everything they can to meet with voters. So, if you are out of commission for any extent of time, it's easy for voters to wonder what's going on," GOP strategist Mark Bednar told Fox News Digital. 

"That being said, if there's a simple explanation like an illness, it's even easier to just prove that outright to voters. If the flu was really the case with Talarico, it's mind-numbing malpractice that his campaign didn't quickly and easily demonstrate that."

Washington Free Beacon investigative reporter Chuck Ross pointed to the Times report Monday, writing on X that the footage "could have been released a week ago and quashed the rumors."

FOX NEWS POLL: IT’S A LONE STAR SENATE SHOWDOWN BETWEEN TALARICO AND PAXTON

Talarico's campaign had maintained throughout his absence that he was recovering from the flu, and Talarico appeared virtually at an event Sept. 30 while visibly ill and told attendees he had come down with the illness. But his extended absence from in-person campaigning increasingly became a subject of speculation as Election Day approached.

The speculation accelerated after Talarico's campaign reposted footage from a February rally on Oct. 3 without initially identifying it as a months-old video. His campaign told the Times it routinely reposts older social media content.

"Let’s be fair here. You’re 20 days out from Election Day, and you’re running for senate in one of the biggest states in the country. Use tech to connect: direct to camera videos, do a livestream. To just go dark is malpractice," Matt Gorman, chief communications officer at Targeted Victory, told Fox News Digital. 

"You’re running for Senate, not some cubicle dweller."

Fox News Digital gave Talarico's campaign an opportunity Tuesday to respond to the criticism and update its previous statement after The New York Times' reporting. The campaign declined to add to its earlier response.

"This is a conspiracy theory that has been proven false. James is excited to be back on the campaign trail after recovering from the flu," campaign spokesperson JT Ennis told Fox News Digital Monday.

item.title: Rory McIlroy inks partnership deal with DP World that includes an unbelievably nice set of perks
item.description: Rory McIlroy's new DP World partnership sends two personalized fitness and recovery trailers to every PGA Tour and DP World Tour event he enters.
item.content:encoded:
Somehow, someway, life just got even better for Rory McIlroy.

The career grand slam winner, who has earned well over $200 million on the golf course alone, has entered into a global partnership with DP World. While athletes joining forces with a company is hardly ever newsworthy, McIlroy teaming up with the logistics company is an exception thanks to the perk that comes along with it.

Moving forward, DP World will be sending not one, but two fitness and recovery trailers to every tournament McIlroy tees it up in on both the DP World Tour and the PGA Tour.

"Rory McIlroy’s season takes him around the world, but his training and recovery environment doesn’t have to change with it," an announcement from DP World stated. "In a new multi-year global partnership announced today, DP World will take McIlroy’s personalised fitness and recovery environment from tournament to tournament, using its smart end-to-end global logistics network to give him and his team greater consistency wherever he competes."

While McIlroy is playing a more limited schedule than ever before in his career, he is still very much a global player, making starts across multiple countries and continents each year.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Sending two fitness trailers around the globe sounds like a nearly impossible challenge, but DP World directly addressed the potential hurdles it may face logistically.

"At the heart of the partnership are two personalised fitness and recovery trailers that will travel with McIlroy across his PGA Tour and DP World Tour schedules," the statement continued. "DP World will manage every stage of their journeys, from collection and customs clearance to storage and delivery, so everything McIlroy needs to train and recover is ready when he arrives at each tournament."

McIlroy has long been one of the leading proponents of fitness in professional golf, and his hours in the gym have resulted in him being among the longest hitters in the game. He's also consistently remained healthy over the years, with his last significant injury taking place in 2017 when he suffered a hairline fracture to his rib cage.

McIlroy made 14 starts on the PGA Tour in 2026, a total that includes each of the four major championships. He's set to make his first start in nearly a month at the DP World India Championship beginning on October 15.
